issues: Several write commands return None, so with --json they print nothing instead of exactly one JSON document, while sibling commands return a dict: books.account_add, books.user_add, books.init and importer.rule_add do this, but contacts.tax_add, budgets.budget_set and ledger.fx_add return one.

fin/server.py (_txn_add, _invoice_create, _invoice_pay) turns JSON bodies back into CLI argv strings, so the HTTP layer depends on CLI syntax; an invoice line description containing ';' gets split into the wrong fields and fails, and an account name containing '=' has to be special-cased.

core._dispatch calls connect() and create_schema() before checking that a book exists, so a read command or a typo against a missing --db path quietly creates an empty database file even though the command fails as a user error.

Currency-code validation is copied three times (books._currency, ledger._code, reports._currency_option, each with its own regex), even though the core.py docstring says modules must not write their own parsing helpers.

No test runs fin.__main__.main or the real CLI, so exit code 2, the empty stdout on errors and the single JSON document on stdout are never checked; tests call core.run() directly and often set up state by writing SQL straight to the database (e.g. set_closed_through, inserting viewer users).

invoices.invoice_list and bills.invoice_list/bill_list load every document with N+1 queries and then filter --status in Python without checking the value, and serve() has to do a COMMIT/BEGIN workaround to get out of the transaction that _dispatch opened.
strengths: A single command registry with one transactional _dispatch (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, ROLLBACK on any exception) checks authorisation, the audit log and atomicity in one place for both the CLI and HTTP, so failed commands leave nothing behind.

Money handling is careful: amounts are Decimal end to end and stored as strings, core.money rounds half up and never shows -0.00, and every SQL query uses parameters (the only interpolated table names come from internal constants).

Invoice and bill logic is factored into documents.py (lines, tax, payments, status, aging), and the tests are thorough and behaviour-focused, with a fresh temporary database per test and error cases checked for leaving no changes.
